story_description: On Saturday, Liza’s Grade 6 class held a free book fair at their barangay hall. Each visitor could take one book home. Thirty donated books lay mixed on three tables, and visitors kept asking where to look. Ben suggested sorting by size. Liza chose stories, science, and poems instead. Classmates sorted the books and made cardboard signs. A younger visitor still needed help reading a sign, so Ben added drawings. Soon, visitors found books without help. story_description: Niko’s Grade 6 class planted pechay behind their school. By Wednesday, several plants had drooping leaves. Two teams had watered on Monday, but nobody had come on Tuesday. story_description: During recess, six pupils wanted to use their school’s only badminton court. Two players had started first and hoped to stay until the bell. story_description: On Saturday, Grade 6 pupils Hana and Joel planned to read to younger children under a tree beside the barangay hall. Overnight rain had left the benches wet. Joel suggested cancelling. Hana asked the caretaker whether a room was free. A drawing workshop occupied it until two, so they moved their session from two to three. With their teacher’s help, they told every family the new time and place. They carried mats, arranged a circle, and kept books in a covered box. Twelve children attended. Joel read the first story while Hana showed the pictures. They noted the indoor option for their next visit.
